projects.name: CANOPY: Adaptive-Granularity Evidence Compression for Multimodal RAG
projects.description: Represents retrieved items as hierarchies and selects evidence at several granularities at once, since choosing a retrieval granularity does not settle how much of each item to keep — cut reader-input evidence tokens by 14.2–27.7% at comparable accuracy across five QA benchmarks over a 33M-item heterogeneous corpus.

projects.name: Hi-Q: Hierarchical Evidence-guided Query Refinement for Multi-Hop Question Answering
projects.description: Grows a query tree whose shape is decided by whether retrieved evidence already supports each unit, rather than by a fixed decomposition template or a pre-built graph — 52.3 EM / 64.0 F1 averaged over three multi-hop QA benchmarks under full-corpus retrieval, 15.1 EM over IRCoT.

projects.name: SPARTA: Scalable and Principled Benchmark of Tree-Structured Multi-hop QA over Text and Tables
projects.description: Automates table-text multi-hop benchmark construction by unifying tables and text into one relational representation and generating nested queries at a target hop count — thousands of QA pairs at a quarter of HybridQA's annotation time, on which models scoring above 70 F1 on HybridQA lose more than 30 F1.

projects.name: Home AI Agent with Event Memory
projects.event: Korean government-hosted AI competition — finalist (top 20 of 1,100+ teams)
projects.description: Merges continuing home-camera scenes into events while preserving observation counts and state transitions, so earlier situations can be recovered without replaying footage — 72 observations into 6 events (91.7% fewer list entries), citing the designated event in 6 of 7 past-event questions.

projects.name: Life-Event-Based Public Service AI Agent
projects.event: Korean government-hosted AI competition — finalist (top 20 of 1,100+ teams)
projects.description: Keeps the user's conditions and completion state as persistent memory and uses it to decide what to surface next across procedures spanning multiple steps and deadlines — 806 procedure items across 50 life events linked by 639 precedence relations, cutting precedence violations from 242 under deadline-only ordering to 0 on a 500-case regression.

projects.name: User Command Prediction for Mobile Flash Translation Layers
projects.description: Predicts the next user command from observed workload patterns so the flash translation layer can prepare for it instead of reacting once the request arrives.
